svg.title: CIA triad: properties, failures and controls
svg.desc: A triangle with confidentiality at the top, integrity at the bottom left and availability at the bottom right. Each corner has a box listing the question it answers, a typical failure and typical controls. The centre reads information security objective.

g.text: Confidentiality: who may see it?
Failure: disclosure to the wrong party
Example: stolen customer database
Controls
Encryption, access control, classification,
MFA, data loss prevention
Integrity: is it still correct and authentic?
Failure: unauthorized or accidental change
Example: altered payment account number
Controls
Hashes, HMAC, digital signatures, input validation,
version control, change management, audit logs,
write-once backups
Availability: can authorized users use it now?
Failure: outage, denial of service, ransomware
Example: DDoS on a public DNS provider
Controls
Redundancy, backups with tested restore, capacity
planning, rate limiting, DDoS mitigation, patching,
disaster recovery with defined RTO and RPO

svg.text: Definitions follow 44 U.S.C. 3542 as quoted in NIST FIPS 199.
